sm: This Evening Wire for Tuesday, November 17th opens with a wave of technology trouble. A cyber attack that ran through the website testing platform Optimizely hit nearly 200 major sites, including CNN, Reuters, Salesforce and Zoom, as hackers tried to steal cryptocurrency and infect Apple devices. Separately, an internal National Security Agency network used for classified information went down, though sources say there is no sign of a cyber attack. The FAA grounded thousands of flights after a glitch, and the FBI warned businesses about software that could be used to disrupt their networks. Former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang agreed to testify before Congress on December 1 over his alleged ties to a Chinese spy. President Trump began his Asia trip in the Philippines before heading to Beijing, and Ukraine knocked down a major section of the Kerch Strait Bridge. Trump said he takes reports of an Iranian dirty bomb plot against Washington very seriously, though the White House says there is no credible threat and Iran calls the claims baseless. A nationwide FEMA emergency alert test fed Simpsons-driven blackout rumors. A judge will unseal parts of the search warrant at Representative Ilhan Omar's home, and Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney died at 95.
sg: Evening news: cyber attacks and Iran
